articles.title: Netflix Turns Infamous Stanford Prison Experiment into Reality Show with ‘30 Willing Participants’
articles.summary: The unscripted series, inspired by the controversial 1971 experiment, premieres Oct. 21
articles.body:
Netflix's new unscripted series will put 30 participants in a real prison as guards and prisoners

The New Stanford Prison Experiment premieres Oct. 21 and will span six episodes

The series is inspired by the controversial 1971 Stanford Prison Experiment

Netflix is putting a reality-TV spin on one of psychology's most infamous experiments.

The streamer is set to debut The New Stanford Prison Experiment , an unscripted series that will place 30 participants inside a real prison and randomly assign them to play either guards or prisoners, per a release shared with PEOPLE.

The six-episode debut season is scheduled to premiere Oct. 21. Alfred Street Industries is producing the series, with Jane Lipsitz, Dan Cutforth, Nan Strait, Dan Volpe, Jeff Grogan and Mike Odair serving as executive producers.

The series will examine what happens when ordinary people are placed within a structured system of power and assigned opposing roles.

"Thirty willing participants enter a real prison and are randomly assigned as guards or prisoners. Thrust into a system of power, hierarchy, and control, they'll discover whether ordinary people inevitably conform to the roles they're given—or whether empathy, morality, and individuality can withstand the forces pushing them in the opposite direction," the synopsis reads, per the release.

"As the pressure builds and the balance of power begins to shift, the central question feels more urgent than ever: Does power corrupt?" the synopsis continues.

For Lipsitz, the project offered an opportunity to revisit a study she had long found compelling.

"The Stanford Prison Experiment has always fascinated me," Lipsitz said. "Despite its serious ethical flaws, it asked a fundamental question that feels even more relevant today: how does power affect ethical choices?"

She described making the series as an intense experience.

"Getting the opportunity to reimagine this social experiment was one of the most intense, exhilarating — and definitely nail-biting — experiences we've ever had," she said.

"Netflix has always been an incredible supporter of ambitious projects that take risks, push boundaries and tell challenging stories, so we were incredibly grateful to have them as our partners on this one," Lipsitz added in the release.

The new series takes its name and central premise from the Stanford Prison Experiment, which was conducted at Stanford University in August 1971. Led by psychology professor Philip G. Zimbardo, the study was designed to examine the psychological effects of authority and powerlessness in a prison setting, according to Stanford University .

Researchers recruited Stanford students through a local newspaper advertisement, ultimately selecting 24 students who were screened and randomly assigned to groups of prisoners and guards, according to the university.

The experiment was initially expected to last one to two weeks but was terminated after just six days as the situation escalated. Prisoners were subjected to cruel and dehumanizing treatment by their fellow students, according to Stanford University.

The experiment became widely known for its findings about the influence of social roles and environments on behavior. Zimbardo described the study as showing how "ordinary college students could do terrible things," according to Stanford University.

A dramatized movie titled The Stanford Prison Experiment was released in 2015, starring Billy Crudup, Michael Angarano and Ezra Miller. The movie was made with Zimbardo's active participation and more closely followed the events of the original study, according to Britannica .

articles.title: Who left 'Dancing With the Stars' last night? 1st celebrity sent home after voting glitch.
articles.summary: Online voting crashed during the Season 35 premiere, forcing the show to count only votes submitted by text.
articles.body:
Dancing With the Stars is back for Season 35 — but one celebrity's bid for the mirror ball trophy has already come to an end.

The ABC show kicked off Tuesday night with a new group of celebrities hoping to follow in the footsteps of Season 34 champion Robert Irwin.

This year's cast includes reality TV stars, actors, athletes, musicians and familiar faces from across the entertainment industry, including Summer House star Ciara Miller, 10 Things I Hate About You actor Julia Stiles, The Traitors ' Maura Higgins and singer Taylor Hanson.

Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli are back at the judges' table, with Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough returning as hosts for their fourth consecutive season.

But after the first round of performances — and the season's first elimination — the competition has already narrowed. So, who was the first celebrity sent home? Here's what happened.

Who was eliminated from 'Dancing With the Stars' last night?

Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Conner Leavitt and professional dance partner Adele Zaikman were the first pair eliminated from Season 35.

Leavitt and Zaikman performed a salsa to Tag Team's "Whoomp! (There It Is)," receiving 4s from all three judges for a total score of 12 out of 30.

"This has been the most fun," Leavitt said after being voted off. "I have the greatest dance partner in the world in Adele. I can't wait for the world to get to see her talent."

Zaikman added, "It's a dream come true no matter what, and I'm so lucky that I had Conner. I had so much fun, and thank you so much for everything."

Leavitt's wife, Whitney, reached the semifinals on DWTS last year. Zaikman joined the lineup after winning the inaugural season of spinoff show Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro .

What happened with 'Dancing With the Stars' voting?

Tuesday night's premiere was hit by technical problems when the show's online voting system crashed during the live broadcast.

Hough initially told viewers that online voting was temporarily unavailable and encouraged them to vote by text. Ribeiro later announced that online votes would be thrown out for the night, meaning only votes submitted by text would count.

Who topped the 'Dancing With the Stars' leaderboard?

Glee star Harry Shum Jr. and professional partner Jenna Johnson finished at the top of the leaderboard Tuesday night, earning 21 out of 30 for their cha cha to Earth, Wind & Fire's "Let's Groove."

Paralympic gold medalist Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach were close behind with 20 points for their tango to Kelly Clarkson's "Since U Been Gone."

The Bachelorette 's Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess scored 17 for their tango to Lenny Kravitz's "Are You Gonna Go My Way," while Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart and Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold each earned 16.

Jackson Olson and Emma Slater scored 15, followed by Leavitt and Zaikman's 12.

Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson finished at the bottom of the judges' leaderboard with 10 points for their cha cha to Jean Knight's "Mr. Big Stuff," but advanced to the next round.

When is 'Dancing With the Stars' on again?

The Season 35 premiere continues Wednesday, Sept. 16, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+, when the female celebrities make their competition debuts.

Following the two-night premiere, Dancing With the Stars will air Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+. Episodes are available to stream the following day on Hulu.

articles.title: iOS 27 is here: 10 iPhone features you’ll want to try now
articles.summary: Safari's Notify Me can monitor websites for price changes and restocks, while new AI photo tools let you reframe and extend shots in iOS 27.
articles.body: Your iPhone is getting a major update. Apple released iOS 27 to the public on Monday, Sept. 14, bringing a wave of new features along with the long-awaited Siri AI beta. However, there is much more happening under the hood. Safari can now watch websites for changes. The Photos app gets powerful new editing tools. Apple also says it has made iOS faster across compatible iPhones. Some of these changes could save you from digging through apps or hunting for information yourself. Others give you more control over how your iPhone looks and works. Here are the iOS 27 features I think are worth trying first, along with how to find them. NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better healthcare With AI In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed. Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com 8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT Will your iPhone get iOS 27? The good news is that Apple kept support fairly broad. iOS 27 works with the iPhone 11 family and newer models. It also supports the second-generation iPhone SE and later. That means plenty of people can upgrade without buying a new phone. However, the biggest AI features have tougher hardware requirements. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max, or an iPhone 16 model or later. So, an iPhone 11 can run iOS 27, but it will miss Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features. Keep in mind that many of the features below, including the new AI photo tools, Safari Notify Me and Call Context, also require an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone. Siri AI is rolling out in beta in English on supported devices. Apple says support for additional languages will follow later. Availability can also vary by region. iOS 27 should also feel faster Apple says iOS 27 brings performance improvements across the system. In Apple's testing, apps can launch up to 30% faster, new photos can load in the Photos app up to 70% faster and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% faster. Apple also says iOS 27 improves transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular connections and makes Mail search more relevant. Those are Apple's own figures, so your results will vary depending on your iPhone and how you use it. How to install iOS 27 on your iPhone Before installing a major update, I recommend backing up your iPhone. Also, connect to Wi-Fi and make sure you have enough battery life or plug your phone into power. Then follow these steps: If iOS 27 does not appear immediately, check again later. Apple software releases can take some time to appear on every compatible iPhone. 1) Reframe a photo after you take it Apple Intelligence moves deeper into the Photos app with Spatial Reframing. It lets you change the composition and perspective of a photo after you took it. Apple Intelligence can generate additional parts of the scene when your new framing exposes areas that were outside the original shot. How to use Spatial Reframing Because AI may create new portions of the scene, I would zoom in and inspect the result before sharing an edited photo. Generative tools can still produce odd details. 2) Extend a photo beyond its original edges Maybe you took a photo too close to your subject. The new Extend tool lets you expand beyond the original edges while Apple Intelligence generates the missing surroundings. How to use Extend in Photos The feature will not work with every photo. Apple also says its intelligent photo-editing tools can be subject to daily usage limits. 3) Clean Up can remove bigger distractions Apple has also upgraded Clean Up in Photos. The tool can now tackle larger unwanted objects and distractions while using AI to fill in the space left behind. How to use Clean Up This could be especially handy for removing a person in the background or another distraction that pulls attention away from the subject. Image Playground gets much more realistic Apple is also giving Image Playground a major upgrade in iOS 27. You can now generate images in many more styles, including photorealistic ones. You can also start with an existing image and describe how you want Apple Intelligence to change it. For example, you could ask it to change the setting or adjust the overall look without starting from scratch. As with Apple’s other generative image tools, usage limits may apply. I would also look closely at the results before sharing them, especially when people or detailed objects appear in the scene. 4) Safari can watch a website for you This may end up being one of my favorite iOS 27 features because it solves a very common frustration. Safari’s new Notify Me feature can monitor a webpage for a change you care about. For example, you could ask Safari to watch for a product coming back in stock. It can also monitor a page for a price change. Instead of reopening the same page over and over, Safari can alert you when something changes. How to use Safari Notify Me You can choose hourly, daily, weekly or monthly checks. However, Notify Me does not yet work on every website. Safari can also automatically organize open tabs by topic, which could help anyone whose browser looks like a digital junk drawer by the end of the week. APPLE AI SECURITY UPDATE PROVES HACKERS MOVE FAST 5) Your iPhone can surface information while you are on a call Apple Intelligence is also getting involved when you call businesses. A new feature called Call Context can surface useful information from other apps while you are on a call. Say you call an airline about a reservation. Call Context can pull up a confirmation code from Mail rather than forcing you to leave the Phone app and search for it while someone waits on the other end. There is no complicated workflow to learn. When you place a supported business call and Apple Intelligence identifies relevant information, it can surface that information during the call. Apple says its system determines what could be useful based on who you are calling. It can do that without analyzing the audio from your call. That is the kind of AI feature I want to see more of because you do not have to change your behavior to benefit from it. 6) Liquid Glass gets a much-needed adjustment Last year, Apple introduced the transparent Liquid Glass design across iOS. Some people liked the new look. Others found certain screens harder to read. With iOS 27, Apple says it has improved contrast and readability. More importantly, you now have greater control over how transparent the interface appears. Apple added a slider that lets you move the look from ultraclear toward fully tinted. How to adjust Liquid Glass The changes appear in real time as you move the slider. The setting applies across iOS, including places such as Control Center, notifications and app overlays. This is a small change, but I like that Apple is giving people a choice rather than assuming one visual treatment works for everyone. 7) Put your favorite Camera controls within easy reach If you are always digging around for the timer, exposure or another Camera setting, iOS 27 lets you keep the controls you use most right above the camera frame. Apple starts you with Flash and Live Photo there, but you can customize the row with other tools you use regularly. How to customize your Camera controls Depending on your iPhone and camera mode, available controls can include Flash, Live Photo, Timer, Exposure, Styles and Aspect. Apple also gives you a Reset to Essentials option if you want to return to the default setup. 8) Parents get more control over what kids can open Apple has put a lot of work into parental controls in iOS 27. The new Ask to Browse feature lets a child request access to a website that has been restricted. The parent receives that request through Messages and can approve or decline it. How to set up Ask to Browse You first need Family Sharing set up with your child in the family group. When your child tries to visit restricted web content, they can send an Ask to Browse request for your approval. Apple has also expanded Communication Safety. It already helps protect children from nudity in supported Apple services. With iOS 27, Apple says the system can intervene when it detects gore or violent content in shared photos and videos. 9) Find My gives you more control over location sharing Find My gets a useful privacy upgrade in iOS 27, especially if you only want someone to see your location for a limited amount of time. You can now choose a custom duration for location sharing or set an exact date and time for it to stop. That could come in handy on a trip, during an event or anytime you want temporary location sharing without having to remember to turn it off later. You can also pause location sharing until the end of the day for specific people. Apple says this can be useful when you want to keep something like a surprise party or gift-shopping trip private. How to use the new Find My location options If you already share your location with someone, you can also pause sharing with that person until the end of the day from their location-sharing options. I like having more control here because location sharing often makes sense for a specific situation. You may want someone to know where you are during a weekend trip without giving them indefinite access afterward. 10) You can describe a Shortcut and let AI build it Shortcuts can be incredibly powerful, but building one manually can get complicated fast. iOS 27 makes the process much easier with Describe a Shortcut. You can tell Apple Intelligence what you want your iPhone to automate in plain English. Shortcuts then connects the actions needed to build it. For example, Apple says you could ask your iPhone to message someone with your ETA when you leave work. You could also build automations that work across supported apps. How to create a Shortcut with a description This could make Shortcuts much more approachable for people who have always liked the idea of automating their iPhone but never wanted to figure out how all the individual actions fit together. Some Shortcuts that rely on Apple’s cloud-based AI models may be subject to daily usage limits. ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS Bonus: Siri AI is here, but it is still in beta This is the feature many iPhone owners have been waiting for, but I would treat it differently from the 10 features above. Siri AI is rolling out as a beta in English on supported devices, so expect some rough edges while Apple continues to improve it. Siri AI can hold more natural conversations and handle follow-up questions. It can also use personal context from information on your device. For example, you could ask Siri to find an old photo without remembering when you took it. You can also ask it to locate something buried in an email or note. Siri can take more actions inside apps, too. Apple says it can work across messages, emails, photos and other supported apps. Siri can also pull information from the web when you ask broader questions. Why you should care The real test will be whether Siri can save you from bouncing between apps. I have always found voice assistants most useful when they remove a few steps from something I already wanted to do. If Siri AI can reliably find a buried email or pull up a photo from years ago based on a vague description, that could change how often people use it. Because this is still a beta, I would double-check important answers or actions before relying on them. How to try the new Siri AI app Apple has also given Siri its own app, which makes it feel more like the AI assistants people have grown used to using. You can also pin conversations you want to keep handy. Apple says you can invoke Siri AI by saying "Hey Siri," pressing the side button or swiping down from the Dynamic Island on supported iPhones. Kurt’s key takeaways What I like most about iOS 27 is that some of its best features solve problems you actually run into. Safari can keep an eye on a webpage so you do not have to. The new photo tools could rescue a shot you thought was unusable. Find My also gives you better control over how long someone can see your location. I am especially interested in what Apple Intelligence can do with Shortcuts. Describing an automation instead of building it action by action could finally make Shortcuts approachable for people who have always found it too complicated. Siri AI is still the feature I will be watching most closely. Apple is asking us to trust Siri with more personal context and more complicated requests, so getting the answers right will be critical. The fact that Siri AI launches as a beta tells me we should expect some bumps along the way. What I want from AI on my iPhone is pretty simple. Save me time without making me think about the technology doing the work. If iOS 27 can consistently do that, these features could become the ones you use every day without even thinking about them. What would Siri AI have to prove before you let it handle more of your day?
